root_idea.summary: The root develops around four related orientations: coming by night, striking or beating, softness or slackening, and placing one layer over another. From these arise notions of roads and ways, successive tracks or layers, nocturnal arrival, and various forms of overlaying or impact.
root_idea.development: The lexical evidence presents the root as a cluster rather than a single uniform meaning. A road may be understood as a beaten or trodden course; night arrival is associated with knocking at a door; and layered or overlaid things motivate meanings involving paths, strata, coverings, folds, and successive arrival.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic noun طَرِيق is a distinct lexical item meaning a path, road, or way.
The Quranic noun طَرِيقَة is a distinct lexical item meaning a way, course, manner, or set of strata.
The Quranic active participle طَارِق is displayed under its normalized singular citation form.

senses.usage_conditions: Used literally for a route or beaten course and also for a figurative way or means. The Quranic occurrences include an indefinite path, a way, and a divinely directed path.

senses.definition: A way, course, manner, practice, or religious orientation; by metonymy, the people or group defined by such a way.
senses.usage_conditions: The word may describe conduct or an established course, whether approved or disapproved. In collective or possessive constructions it can denote a group adhering to a way, including differing sects or an eminent body of people. The Quranic usages include conduct, a people's way, and the way or course being followed.

senses.definition: A series of layers or stages arranged one above another; specifically, strata or levels of the heavens.
senses.usage_conditions: This plural-oriented usage describes successive superposed levels rather than a traveled road. It is explicitly applied to the seven heavenly strata.

senses.definition: One who or something that comes by night; specifically, the star that appears at night.
senses.usage_conditions: The active-participial sense is conventionally specialized to a nocturnal comer. In the Quranic passage it refers to the night-appearing star, also explained as the morning star because of its appearance toward the end of the night.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Striking, beating, pounding, or knocking; an act of hitting with the hand, a stick, or a hammer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes knocking at a door, beating wool or hair to loosen it, striking iron, and slapping. The same verbal root can describe beating a surface or road with the feet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To travel or tread a road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of beating or treading a track; the object may be the road itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Coming or arriving by night; by extension, a sudden nocturnal visitation or occurrence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person, star, apparition, anxiety, calamity, or other event arriving at night or descending suddenly as though knocking at a door.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a male animal, to cover a female for mating.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence especially illustrates a stallion camel covering a she-camel; the construction is a sexual or mating use, not a general meaning of road or travel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Divination by striking or arranging pebbles, sand, or marks.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes pessomancy and related forms of geomantic or sand divination, traditionally associated with diviners and sometimes women.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To practice or undertake divination, especially pebble divination.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived verbal use associated with the practice of divination or related artifice.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To brand a ewe with the mark called طِرَاق.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized livestock-marking use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become weak in intellect and soft or yielding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a passive or stative verbal use, distinct from the ordinary physical meaning of striking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have weakness or crookedness in the knees, arm, foreleg, or leg.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a human being or camel; one description concerns crookedness in the ساق without the condition called فَحَج.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To drink turbid or muddy water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The water is water in which animals have waded, urinated, or defecated and which has consequently become cloudy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a road or passage level, usable, or available; to give or admit a way to someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes making a route passable and granting access. The construction may also be used of making a way for animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To begin bringing forth by making a passage, with the young partly emerging and then becoming temporarily stuck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a pregnant woman or female animal; the evidence also applies a related image to a bird making a place for laying eggs. The defining feature is partial emergence followed by obstruction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To acknowledge another person's right or due after previously denying it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional figurative construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To withhold camels from pasture or from something they would otherwise approach.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare, authority-attributed lexical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sew one layer of material over another, as in doubling a shield, sole, or skin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction describes reinforcement by attaching a matching second layer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To place or sew one thing over another; to put one garment, coat of mail, or sole over another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III construction that may involve a single agent; the resulting arrangement is superposed or doubled.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For clouds to follow upon darkness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use of successive arrival or following.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To employ varied modes or styles in speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction meaning to take up different manners or techniques of expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lend someone a stallion for covering his she-camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative livestock-breeding construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To provide or cause a person to have a mate or sexual partner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Preserved as a specialized idiomatic or supplicatory construction; the source uses the language of marriage or sexual intercourse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lower or incline the head, lower the eyes, or become silent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May describe a physical lowering of the head or gaze, natural laxness of the eyelids, silence from fear, or a deliberate lowering of the eyes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To incline toward diversion, sport, or play.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use of inclination.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To set a snare or trap for game.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to beasts or birds of the chase.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To plot against someone through calumny or slander in order to bring about his ruin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of setting a snare.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To find a way to something or seek access to it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Usually followed by إلى and describing approach by a means or route.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come consecutively or follow one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of camels, darkness, clouds, or tidings arriving in succession; a secondary reported use describes dispersal along different roads.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To overlay or become arranged in successive layers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a bird's feathers, layers of earth compacted by rain, deposits in a tank, or night coming portion upon portion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To request or demand a stallion for breeding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form X request construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To request divination by pebbles and the diviner's interpretation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized request construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek, take, or travel a road or passage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes taking a way between ranks or along a route to a door, and taking a portion as a passage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tune, melody, or musical air played on the lute or a similar instrument.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may also refer to a kind or variety of musical sound.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stallion camel that covers females.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized or epithetic use of the verbal notion of covering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The reproductive fluid of a stallion camel, and by extension sometimes of a man; also the fee for a camel's covering.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence treats the stallion's covering as the original association and reports human application as figurative or epithetic.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Turbid or stagnant water in which animals have waded, urinated, or defecated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May denote rainwater or other collected water, or places where such water gathers in stony land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A snare, trap, or net used to catch wild animals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes a hunter's snare comparable to a فَخّ or حِبَالَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind of palm tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal botanical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fatness, and consequently strength or vigor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Often occurs in the negative expression meaning that a person or camel has no fat or strength.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rendered submissive, tractable, or broken.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to a beast.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A row of bricks, palm trees, or other things arranged in a line.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective or unit noun for an ordered row.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A track or line of footprints, especially the single track made by camels following closely one after another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The emphasis is on successive marks lying along one route.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fold or doubling of a waterskin or similar object.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural denotes the folds produced when the skin is bent or doubled.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Overlapping folds or layers of the belly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bodily anatomical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The condition of feathers overlying one another; in some descriptions, softness or flaccidity of feathers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive use for birds' feathers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One time or one occurrence; an occasion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for repeated occurrences, such as doing something once or twice, and in comparisons meaning times over.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The main, middle, or distinct beaten track of a road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized road expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The work or manufacture of one person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of objects, such as arrows, made by a single craftsman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A way, course, custom, habit, or manner of being.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This broader Classical use includes a person's habitual practice or state, whether good or bad.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A line, streak, or stripe in a layered or marked object.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to sewn materials, bows, and similar objects.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Stones or other objects lying one upon another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A layered-arrangement use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Darkness, especially the darkness of night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Appears in an expression for arriving during the darkness of night.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Inordinate desire or something coveted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare lexical use reported with two closely related interpretations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A specified unnatural or effeminate vice.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An attributed, specialized use; it is not a general meaning of way or custom.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Foolish, stupid, or deficient in understanding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use applied to a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Prey or a hunted object.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare meaning reported from a poetic lexicographical source.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An arrangement of things one upon another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression describes placing objects in successive layers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who journeys by night, especially to reach his household at night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May also describe one who travels frequently by night.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sole sewn onto another sole to make a doubled sandal or shoe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The added sole is made to match the first closely.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The leather sole of a sandal after its thong has been removed; also a round piece of skin attached to a shield.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence includes applications to the soles attached to camels' feet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Anything made to match or correspond with another thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A generalized extension from a matching additional layer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Expanded or rounded iron used for a helmet, armlet, or layered armor plates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes plates of a helmet arranged one above another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A white brand or line made by fire on the middle of a ewe's ear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Two such marks may be called طِرَاقَانِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A road-related expression involving wayfarers, road duties, or interception of a road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes idioms for the people of the road, duties owed on a road, and making a road dangerous by robbery or violence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A highway robber.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative road expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Devotees or people dedicated to a religious way.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional figurative expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The hyena.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed zoological expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Branches of a road that diverge and lead in different directions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural idiom based on branching roads.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The space between two rows of palm trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A spatial extension based on the elongated course of a road.

other_classical_meanings.definition: With the stronger reason; a fortiori.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later conventional phrase rather than a basic physical meaning of road.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind or variety of palm tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical use distinct from the figurative meaning way or course.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel covered by a stallion, or one that has reached the suitable age for covering; by metaphor, a wife.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It is not required that the she-camel has already been covered; the wife use is a metaphorical extension.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land capable of receiving and absorbing rainwater.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metaphor from the female capable of being impregnated or affected by the male.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The vicissitudes or changing courses of time and fortune.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative plural use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The air or tune of a song.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source identifies this as probably post-Classical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A line, streak, stripe, crease, wrinkle, seam, vein, strip, or elongated portion of a material.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to backs, rocks, sand, fat, flesh, cloth, and similarly extended forms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Strips or shreds, as of a worn-out garment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative plural based on lines or strips.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lines or wrinkle-like streaks in a spear shaft dried by shrinking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The last remaining soft or best portions of pasture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural specialized to residual grazing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A declivity, channel, border, side, or edge of the ground, cloth, or a layered object.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source preserves uncertainty over the exact reading of one ground term; the securely reported branch concerns an edge or border of something composed of parts or colors.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A narrow woven web of wool or hair sewn into the meeting place of tent sections.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical tent-making term; the tent-pole heads pass between these strips.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tent pole.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical architectural use for one of the poles of a tent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tall, very tall, smooth, or hand-reachable palm tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal botanical use with several reported specifications.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who lowers his eyes or keeps silent much or often.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person; the feminine substantive may denote gentleness, submissiveness, or affected languor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The male of the bird called كَرَوَان.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is explained by the bird's falling to the ground and becoming silent when it sees a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Soft or level ground made easy to travel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The image is of ground beaten level and trodden by feet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Gentleness, submissiveness, softness, flaccidity, or languor in a person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantive use that can also imply weakness or affected gentleness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An antidote or theriac.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical variant equated with تِرْيَاقٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A chief or eminent person, metaphorically likened to a lofty star.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Appears in the expression “daughters of a Ṭāriq,” meaning daughters of a chief or king.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A diviner, especially one who practices divination with pebbles.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized substantive distinct from the nocturnal-comer sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man's small tribal subdivision, such as a clan or sub-tribe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized kinship term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small couch large enough for one person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal use from Yemen.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large mace or similar defensive implement, according to one lexical interpretation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source records scholarly disagreement with an alternative derivation as cuirasses; the mace interpretation is retained as reported evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A necklace or a type of necklace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized ornamental noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An early-bearing variety of palm tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Described as a Hijazi palm whose dates ripen before those of other palms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Covered or reinforced by another layer sewn over it, especially a shield or sole.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may consist of two skins or of skin and sinew arranged one above another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Low, ignoble, or mean in lineage or claim to honor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person and distinct from the physical lowering-of-the-eyes sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An enemy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative substantive derived from plotting against someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rod, stick, or hammer used for beating wool, hair, iron, or a person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes the blacksmith's hammer and the implement used to loosen wool or hair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Stamped or minted, as of gold.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial use meaning marked or struck into form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel rendered tractable, submissive, or manageable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative passive-participial use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Marked with lines, streaks, or bands of different colors.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a horse-cloth or similar patterned object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bird that has reached the time when its egg is about to emerge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied specifically in the cited evidence to the bird called قَطَاة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel recently covered by a stallion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized livestock term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Camels coming in one track or following one another closely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may emphasize a single road or successive approach to water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: That which follows something, or resembles it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantive expression based on succession and likeness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: People going on foot without riding animals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural use with a reported singular variant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One whom everyone beats or slaps.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial use that also motivates figurative meanings of being subdued or disabled.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Herbage struck by rain after having dried up.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized agricultural or pastoral use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Mineral substances.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized plural noun reported without further semantic development in the entry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Quickness of pace or going.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical noun or epithet describing rapid movement or a quick pace.

cautions: The Quranic interpretation of طَرِيقَتِكُمْ in 20:63 includes both an established way or religious system and, by metonymy, the people associated with it; both readings are retained under one sense because the lexical branch is the same.
The Quranic plural طَرَائِق in 23:17 is represented as superposed heavenly strata, while the related Quranic usages in 72:11 and 72:16 concern ways, courses, or groups defined by a way.

Some rare Classical meanings are attributed to individual authorities or preserved with textual uncertainty, especially the ground term associated with طَرِيقَةٌ and the interpretation of طَوَارِق as maces; these qualifications are retained in the relevant entries.
